conclusions: ASCII and MAT EMG values are numerically equivalent at source decimal precision for every assessable frozen subject; official source absence remains explicit for Participants 6 and 7.
C3D marker trajectories are equivalent for most subjects, while source-level discrepancies in Participants 14-16 are detected and quarantined.
C3D EMG is time-aligned but not amplitude-equivalent to the official ASCII/MAT representation in assessable subjects and is therefore quarantined from direct numeric interchangeability.
Raw event annotations are absent from all compared representations; this absence is retained and is not imputed.
limitations: The experiment validates one fixed speed and trial per subject, not every recording in the release.
C3D EMG discordance is detected and bounded descriptively; its vendor-export cause is not inferred from the files alone.
Event fidelity cannot be estimated because the raw source representations contain no event annotations for the frozen recordings.

protocol_interpretation.decision_rule: all assessable ASCII-MAT equivalence controls must pass; every C3D comparison must be classified by the frozen source-precision threshold and non-equivalent representations must be quarantined

discordance_freeze.rationale: C3D EMG waveforms are time-aligned but exceed source-precision amplitude tolerance; direct numeric interchangeability must be rejected rather than silently assumed
